title: 172nd Infantry Brigade Multimodal Transportation
description: Package about how with a deployment in the near future the 172nd Infantry Brigade must start to move its equipment to Afghanistan.  Sgt. Collin Black takes us to Mihail Kogalniceanu Airfield Romania to show us how the 21st Theater Sustainment Command and its subordinate units tackles the task of equipment transportation.  Soundbites include Chief Warrant Officer Cheryl Moore - Transportation Operations Mobility Warrant, Hometown: Gulf Port, Miss., Lt. Col. John Platte - Deployed Commander, 615th Contingency Response Element, Hometown: Alexandria, Va., and Capt. Brant Leyden - MK Airfield 16th Sustainment Brigade OIC, Hometown: Springfield, Va.  Produced by Army Sgt. Collin Black, Hometown: Lancaster, Ohio.
keywords: 172nd Infantry Brigade, 21st Theater Sustainment Command, Brant Leyden, Mihail Kogalniceanu Airfield, Collin Black, Cheryl Moore, John Platte, Romania Logistics, Afghanistan, Romania, logistics

transcript.text: The equipment of units deploying to Afghanistan traditionally moves through Pakistan via convoy.
In an effort to mitigate the risks associated with convoying equipment,
the 21st Theater Systemic Command, in conjunction with the Air Force,
try a new supply route, where equipment makes a stop in MK Airfield Romania before it's flown directly to Afghanistan.
When the cargo was moved by rail from Germany to MK,
essentially what happened at that point was the 24st TSC prepared the cargo for air shipment
by placing it on pallets and chaining it down to those pallets.
Then they transported over to the airfield into our cargo yard for the Air Force side,
where my airman worked jointly with the Army to inspect that cargo and make sure it's ready for shipment on the 747s you see behind me.
The movement eliminates the need for convoys through Pakistan, but still has many moving parts.
It is known to the soldiers as a multi-modal move, which means several types of transport are used at once.
Luckily in this area that we have, we have different transportation support.
We have trucks, rail, boats, air, everything that we need to do, any kind of operations that we'd like to do,
going into the deployment or redeployment locations.
After the equipment is finished being inspected and palletized, the final step is loading the equipment onto a Boeing 747.
Each 747 is bound directly for Afghanistan and can carry up to 33 pallets of equipment.
21st TSC and 16th Sustainable Brigade, this is a priority mission for us,
in that this is helping the real world personnel.
This is not a training mission, this is us supporting the warfighters for operation enduring freedom.
So this is making sure that the warfighters get the support that they need.
This operation marks the first time deploying equipment is being moved through MK Airfield.
For 21st TSC Public Affairs, I'm Army Sergeant Colin Black, MK Airfield, Romania.
